description: Machine-readable documentation QUALITY standards (thresholds + severities) for managed repositories. README section contracts are NOT defined here; they live in ai-doc-templates.json (readmeTemplates[].requiredSections), which is canonical. This file references the canonical universal baseline and applies severity/threshold policy on top of it.

sectionAuthority.note: Validators resolve required sections by (a) selecting a profile, then using that profile's requiredSections, or (b) falling back to universalSections when no profile is known. Do not hardcode section lists here.

requiredRootFiles.name: README.md
requiredRootFiles.recommendedAction: Create a README.md with project description, installation steps, and usage guide.

requiredRootFiles.name: LICENSE
requiredRootFiles.recommendedAction: Add a LICENSE file to clarify terms of use.

requiredRootFiles.name: CONTRIBUTING.md
requiredRootFiles.recommendedAction: Add CONTRIBUTING.md to guide contributors on how to submit changes.

requiredRootFiles.name: CHANGELOG.md
requiredRootFiles.recommendedAction: Add CHANGELOG.md to document notable changes between versions.

readmeStandards.minLengthRecommendedAction: Expand README.md to at least 300 characters with meaningful project information.

sectionPolicy.description: Severity applied per missing section. Which sections are 'expected' comes from the canonical templates, not from a list here. A missing universal section is a warning; a missing profile-specific (non-universal) section is info.
sectionPolicy.recommendedActionTemplate: Add a {section} section as required by the {profile} README profile.

readmeStandards.minLengthSeverityRationale: Critical, not warning, since 2026-08-20. A README below the minimum is not untidy - it is insufficient CONTEXT for an agent, which the product direction names as a standing risk ("README quality may be insufficient for meaningful Copilot context"). It therefore belongs with a MISSING README as a dispatch blocker, and apart from doc-hygiene warnings like a missing LICENSE, which say nothing about whether an agent can work the roadmap safely. This distinction is the reason the severity gate can block on critical alone without letting context-poor repositories through.

docFindingSeverityGate.rationale: Which doc-finding severities may FREEZE dispatch, declared here because until 2026-08-20 the rule lived only in code and contradicted this file: the scanner blocked on any warning OR critical, while these rules named only a missing README. The effect on the real portfolio was that seven repositories with contract-quality roadmaps and real pending work were undispatchable because they lacked a LICENSE file - a warning with no bearing on whether an agent can safely do roadmap work. Criticals still block; warnings and info are reported on the repo and do not gate. Widen `blocks` to re-tighten without a code change.
